Plot the STABL Stability Path

Source: R/visualization.R
plot_stabl_path.Rd

Produces a ggplot2 line chart showing the stability score (frequency of selection) of each feature across the regularisation path. Selected features are highlighted in red; noise features are shown in dark grey. When artificial features were used during fitting, their stability path is overlaid as thin dotted grey lines. The FDP+-optimal (or hard) threshold is shown as a dashed horizontal line.

Usage

plot_stabl_path(
  object,
  new_hard_threshold = NULL,
  title = "STABL Stability Path"
)

Arguments

object

A fitted "stabl_fit" object from stabl_fit().

new_hard_threshold

Numeric in (0, 1] or NULL. When supplied, overrides the threshold stored in object.

title

Character; plot title (default "STABL Stability Path").

Value

A ggplot object.

Details

When the lambda grid contains an alpha column (elastic-net mixed-alpha path), the plot is automatically faceted by alpha.

The path is always drawn in decreasing-lambda order (high penalty on the left, low penalty on the right) within each alpha level, independently of the row order of the supplied lambda grid. The x-axis is the position along that ordered path, so auto grids (log-spaced lambda) are evenly spaced.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(1L)
  x <- matrix(rnorm(40 * 6), 40, 6,
               dimnames = list(paste0("s", 1:40), paste0("f", 1:6)))
  y <- setNames(rnorm(40), rownames(x))
  fit <- stabl_fit(x, y,
                   lambda_grid = data.frame(lambda = c(0.3, 0.1, 0.05)),
                   n_bootstraps = 6L, hard_threshold = 0.3, random_state = 1L)
  plot_stabl_path(fit)
}
